items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: I went down to, uh, Pete Herman's. Played down there with, uh, Bebe Ridgely.

ctx.x: I was playing clarinet. I was doing clarinet. And what about the name of Earl? His name was Earl Trusclair. He's the first man that ever showed me any finger on a saxophone. We alternated. He showed me my finger on the saxophone and I showed him his finger on the clarinet. And that's the only thing anybody ever showed me about a saxophone. Oh, no. Nobody never showed me nothing about a clarinet, but on the saxophone, that's the only fella ever showed me anything. He showed me how to finger it. And other than…

broke up? Oh, well, Solistan made up his own band. I mean, on the trumpet, when Ridgely. Shatz. Shatz. And was he playing with you at the Pete Hermans? Who, Shatz? Yeah, I forget who you said was there. Yeah, Shatz was on trumpet at Pete Hermans. Uh-huh. Mm-hmm. Okay, he was playing trumpet. What else? I was wondering about, uh, did you ever meet Charlie Parker around Kansas City or St. Louis or any of those places?
